problem: VLN-CE methods are trained and evaluated in simulation and transfer poorly to the real world because of the visual domain gap and lack of prior environment knowledge. Foundation-model navigation methods like VLMaps/LM-Nav need a pre-collected offline map or data of the environment.
motivation: Real robots must follow natural-language instructions in unseen environments where no prior mapping is possible. Large foundation models (LLM, VLM) generalize to real-world observations, so combining them with online mapping could avoid sim training and real-world fine-tuning.
key_idea: Parse instructions with an LLM into macro-actions, build an online LSeg-based visual-language map, ground each macro-action's landmark to a map waypoint by language indexing, and execute it with a pretrained DD-PPO point-goal controller, all without training.
insight: Replacing a sim-trained learned grounding module (CM2) with foundation models (LLM parser + LSeg map) while keeping the same DD-PPO controller isolates the visual domain gap as the failure cause: CM2 gets 0% SR on the complex instruction vs 100% for the proposed method. Online mapping plus choosing the nearest landmark in front of the robot mitigates object ambiguity. There is no formal ablation; the evidence is the head-to-head comparison with a shared controller.
method: Instruction parser: GPT-3.5 with few-shot prompts converts the instruction into a sequence of 10 pre-defined macro-action descriptions (Python dicts with name and landmark/distance parameters).
Online visual-language mapper: back-projects RGB-D with LSeg pixel-wise features into a 5 cm-resolution 2D grid map, updated every step by averaging features per cell, using relative pose.

Language indexing-based localizer: computes map-feature/text-embedding similarity with LSeg text encoder to get a semantic map, runs DBSCAN to find landmark centers, and picks the nearest one in front of the robot as the waypoint.
Pure motion handling: for move/turn macro-actions with no landmark, the waypoint is computed geometrically from the current pose and the distance (default 0.5 m).
DD-PPO local controller: an off-the-shelf pretrained point-goal policy takes RGB-D and the polar waypoint (rho, phi) and outputs forward/left/right/stop.

setting.observation: front-view RGB-D (640x480) plus relative pose from odometry, known camera intrinsics
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 15°, stop

numbers.eval_set_note: 4 instructions x 5 runs in an unseen lab
1 complex instruction, 5 runs from different start locations

numbers_note: Only small-scale real-world experiments (no standard benchmark). Pure-motion results in Table 1 give actual distance travelled, not SR. The text says 0.2 m mean distance for Ours while Table 2 average says 0.66.
results: In a real unseen lab, the method reaches 95% average SR on single landmark instructions vs 30% for CM2, and 100% SR on a complex multi-step instruction vs 0% for CM2 (0.256 m vs 4.9 m distance to goal, 88.6 vs 203.4 steps). It uses no training or fine-tuning.
limitations: Grounding is bounded by the small set of 10 pre-defined macro-action descriptions, limiting complex instructions.
The localizer favors explicit landmarks or absolute movements and struggles with coarse, high-level instructions.
Evaluation is tiny (a few instructions, 5 runs each, one lab, one baseline) and not on standard VLN-CE benchmarks.
